as_told.title: Malmgren in the Cuban Missile Crisis war room confronts Curtis LeMay

plain: During the Cuban missile crisis of 1962, a young adviser named Harold Malmgren, then around 26 or 27, was sent by Kennedy into "the tank", a secure Pentagon meeting room, to "stall" the Air Force general Curtis LeMay and keep him from possibly launching nuclear weapons, according to Matthew Pines, a guest who says Malmgren told him so. Malmgren tells Michels the story himself, naming Defense Secretary Robert McNamara and adviser McGeorge Bundy as present, and recalls arguing "it's madness": if you hit Moscow, "there's no one to talk to" to stop a war once started.
